cells.tense: Right now you're picking up what's true about the people in front of you, and it holds up.
cells.ask: Offer the pattern you already see in what someone's carrying — one clear sentence, said out loud.
cells.core:
You walk into a room and its shape is just there for you. Who's holding back, who's about to say the hard thing, what's actually going on under the talk — you get it without working for it. That's not a skill you're performing. It's how you arrive.

What it gives the people around you is steadiness. When you say what you notice, things settle — not because you've fixed anything, but because someone finally named it. You can trust your read of people the way you trust your own hands. So say the true thing once, in one clean sentence, and let it land on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You see what's true in people and they feel steadier for it.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once
cells.place: in the place where you meet other people and find your footing alongside them

cells.tense: You're already three conversations ahead, bracing for what people might say before they've opened their mouths.
cells.ask: Spend one conversation with nothing prepared — no angle, no plan for where it should land — and let the direction come from what's actually in the room.
cells.core:
You walk in already knowing what they'll say, what they'll need, where it's going — and you're managing all of it before it happens. The reading that used to be a gift has turned into a head start you can't switch off. You're holding everyone's next move and calling it being prepared.

The plain seeing is still in you, and you can tell when it's clean: someone tells you something and you just take it in, no plan required. Pick one direction instead of all of them. Let one conversation go wherever it actually goes, and let yourself be surprised by it.
cells.sheetLine: You're pre-reading everyone instead of actually meeting them.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once
cells.place: in the place where you meet other people and find your footing alongside them

cells.tense: Something in you stopped trusting what you pick up from people, and you've been running on that since.
cells.ask: Put one picture of what you actually want from someone into words — rough, unfinished — and let that pull you toward them instead of waiting to be sure.
cells.core:
You used to walk into a room and just know how it was. That's quiet now. You watch people and get nothing back, or you get something and talk yourself out of it before you act. The instrument works — it's just unplugged.

When it's connected, you feel someone's state and it moves you toward them instead of away from them. Nothing has to be decided first; the pull does the deciding. So don't try harder to read the room. Name one thing you want from one person — the actual want, not the safe version — and let that wanting do the looking.

cells.tense: You're already reading what's fair and what's owed in every exchange you're in — you just don't call it that.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did because it was right, not because anyone asked, and own that read as yours.
cells.core:
In a room where things are even, you feel it in your body before you think anything. Someone gives, someone receives, nothing's being counted, and you're at ease in it — that's the signal you steer by, and it's accurate more often than you'd admit. You've been calibrating fairness in every room you walk into — noticing who's giving more, who's owed something, what would make it right — and calling it just being reasonable. It's instinct, not calculation. It's running whether you claim it or not.

When it's honest, exchange feels easy: you give, you receive, the ledger stays closed. You can feel the difference between that ease and the quiet tally that starts when something's off. Say out loud about one thing, 'I did that because it was right,' and let that read be yours.
